incidents.weather_conditions: Severe ash blizzard, -34°C, wind gusts 80 km/h, visibility 8 meters
incidents.title: The Figure at Perimeter Post 4
incidents.log_entry: 03:14 — Infrared periscope sweep detected a narrow thermal signature standing motionless beside Perimeter Post 4, approximately sixty meters from the outer blast seal. Target did not crouch against the gale or attempt to shield its face. Through the 4x optical sight, the outline appeared to be a tall person wearing a long pre-war greatcoat with no respirator or hood. Target remained stationary for twenty-eight minutes while the wind blew horizontally. At 03:42, a heavy gust of snow obscured the sight for six seconds. When the glass cleared, the perimeter was completely empty. At dawn, we inspected Post 4 on a tether line: there were no footprints in the snow, no disturbance in the ash crust, and the barbed wire had not been touched. My hands shook while tightening the periscope gland nut.
incidents.tactical_action: Increased cupola floodlight interval; logged in red ink.

incidents.weather_conditions: Clear frozen night, -41°C, calm air, heavy ground inversion haze
incidents.title: The Ghost Engines on Highway 9
incidents.log_entry: 23:45 — A deep, low-frequency rumble was heard approaching along the abandoned embankment of Highway 9 from the north. Sound profile matched a column of four or five heavy diesel transport trucks idling in low gear. Vibration registered on the bunker's lower geophones at 14 Hz. Sentry swept the highway with the high-intensity searchlight: the asphalt was broken, cracked with frost heaves, and blocked by three overturned tank cars. Nothing was moving. Yet the sound of diesel engines idling and exhaust manifolds creaking in the cold passed directly in front of our observation slit, moved south across the frozen river bridge, and faded toward Sector 12 over twenty minutes. Sentry did not fire.
incidents.tactical_action: Geophone gain recalibrated; no physical hostiles engaged.

incidents.weather_conditions: Dense chemical ground fog, -26°C, zero wind
incidents.title: Three Slow Knocks on Blast Door 1
incidents.log_entry: 05:22 — Exactly three heavy, rhythmic impacts occurred against the outside face of Blast Door 1. The sound was not a ricochet or ice falling from the intake hood; it was deliberate, spaced at precise two-second intervals, delivered with an iron tool or heavy ring. Through the periscope glass, the vestibule step was entirely vacant. The snow in front of the door was undisturbed, showing only the frozen furrows left by our last patrol three days ago. Dosimeter probe against the outer door plate showed a momentary spike from 0.05 mSv/h to 1.8 mSv/h that decayed within forty seconds back to baseline. Sentry did not open the hatch.
incidents.tactical_action: Inner bolts locked; secondary airlock interlock engaged.

incidents.weather_conditions: Light acid drizzle, -18°C, freezing rain forming glaze ice
incidents.title: Pulsing Light in the Flooded Grain Silo
incidents.log_entry: 01:10 — Sentry observed a steady, emerald-green light pulsing at twelve beats per minute from the upper cupola window of Grain Silo #3, two kilometers across the drowned flats. Silo #3 has been flooded under three meters of canal mud since Day 40 and has no electrical feed. Light was monochromatic, approximately 532 nm wavelength (diode or emergency laser). Pulse pattern continued without interruption for two hours and forty minutes, then ceased precisely at 03:50. We attempted to raise the silo on all radio frequencies; received only rhythmic click-train static on 88.4 MHz. No scouting party authorized due to sub-zero acid mud.
incidents.tactical_action: Coordinates logged on master chart; scouting prohibited.

incidents.title: Human Speech in the Air Duct
incidents.log_entry: 20:05 — While inspecting the secondary rock-wool particulate filter on Intake Duct B, sentry heard clear, low human whispers originating from inside the 600mm welded steel intake pipe. Voice was male, speaking in a rapid, flat monotone, reciting long lists of five-digit numbers and names of pre-war railway junctions. Sentry tapped three times on the pipe with a spanner; the whispering immediately stopped. After four seconds of silence, a voice inside the pipe whispered: 'Stepan, check the turnbuckle on the third beam.' Sentry disassembled the intake grille: the pipe was dry, free of tracks, and blocked sixty meters up by an intact bird screen. Sentry checked the third beam in Sector 4 and found the turnbuckle cracked halfway through. Sentry did not speak of this to the shift.
incidents.tactical_action: Turnbuckle replaced immediately; intake duct welded shut.

incidents.weather_conditions: Overcast grey sky, -22°C, light ash flurry
incidents.title: Unidentified Birds Flying South
incidents.log_entry: 07:15 — Sentry observed a dense flock of approximately two hundred large black birds flying in strict V-formation south-southwest across the valley at three hundred meters altitude. Flock made zero audible sound — no wingbeats, no calls, no cries. Through 8x binoculars, their silhouettes were ragged, with missing primary feathers and trailing white filaments resembling frayed asbestos insulation. They flew directly through the high-radiation plume above the old transformer substation without breaking formation or altering heading. No bird has been seen alive in Tessarat since the exchange. Sentry watched them disappear into the southern cloud bank. Sentry felt a profound cold in the chest.

incidents.weather_conditions: Minus thirty-eight degrees, dead calm, clear starry frost
incidents.title: Spontaneous Blue Flame on Mile 14
incidents.log_entry: 02:40 — A pillar of pale blue flame erupted from the center of the asphalt intersection at Mile Post 14, three kilometers northeast. Flame burned with a silent, steady hiss, approximately four meters high, emitting intense ultraviolet glow on our periscope sensors but zero smoke or soot. Flame burned for seventeen minutes, then vanished instantly like a gas burner switched off. Sentry inspected the location on morning ski patrol: the asphalt was cold, with no scorch marks, no melted snow, and the frost on the weeds was completely intact. But a pocket dosimeter left on the exact spot discharged completely within two minutes.
incidents.tactical_action: Marked as Gamma Hotspot 14; bypass route established.

incidents.title: Fresh Tracks Ending in Open Snow
incidents.log_entry: 15:30 — Sentry discovered a single set of fresh snowshoe tracks crossing the frozen canal basin heading toward the lock gate. The tracks were crisp, made within the past two hours in fresh powder, showing the distinctive diamond weave of military rawhide shoes. Sentry tracked the trail for four hundred meters across the wide, level snowfield. In the exact center of the open basin, three hundred meters from any tree or structure, the tracks simply stopped. No jump marks, no struggle, no ski tracks, no helicopter rotor wash, no disturbance in the surrounding powder. Just a clean pair of snowshoe impressions in the snow, and then virgin white drifts for half a kilometer in every direction.
incidents.tactical_action: Trail photographed and flagged; no body recovered.

incidents.weather_conditions: High static electrical storm, -20°C, howling wind
incidents.title: Magnetic Inversion Event
incidents.log_entry: 21:15 — All magnetic compasses in the cupola and surface shelter began spinning erratically at 120 rpm. Within five minutes, the needles settled pointing exactly south-southeast with strong magnetic pull. Simultaneously, the steel guy wires on the radio mast began glowing with bright blue corona discharge (St. Elmo's fire), and the generator voltmeter showed sixty volts of induced potential across the grounded intake casing. Through the periscope, the horizon appeared distorted, as if viewed through thick bottle glass. Event lasted forty-four minutes before magnetic north abruptly snapped back to true. Generator bearings inspected: no mechanical damage, but all hand tools on the bench became permanently magnetized.
incidents.tactical_action: Tools degaussed; event logged with telemetry vault.

incidents.weather_conditions: Dense mountain rime frost, -36°C, total fog
incidents.title: Sound of Footsteps Inside the Shell
incidents.log_entry: 03:40 — Sentry stationed inside the maintenance tunnel of the ruined summit radar sphere heard slow, barefoot footsteps pacing along the aluminum catwalk fifteen meters overhead. Sentry aimed the sealed beam lantern: the catwalk was empty, coated in three inches of undisturbed frost. As the light struck the reflector dish, the sound of quiet, rhythmic weeping echoed from the fiberglass dome, moving slowly around the perimeter of the sphere. Sentry challenged three times: 'Identify yourself by sector badge!' The weeping stopped. A single small pebble of frozen condensation fell from the catwalk and struck sentry's helmet. Sentry completed the watch with rifle at low ready.
incidents.tactical_action: Summit maintenance tunnel barred from inside.

incidents.title: Force on the Surface Guide Line
incidents.log_entry: 13:25 — Sentry was conducting a scheduled safety tether check along the fifty-meter steel cable connecting the airlock to the fuel storage vault. Sentry felt three sharp, violent tugs on the safety line from the darkness ahead. Sentry stopped and called on the field intercom: 'Anton, is that you on the line?' No response on radio. Sentry felt the cable slowly pull taut with immense force, as if a heavy vehicle or large animal was hauling the line away into the snow. The 8mm galvanized cable stretched until the turnbuckle groaned. Sentry unclipped the carabiner and backed toward the airlock door with 12-gauge shotgun ready. After twenty seconds, the tension vanished and the cable dropped slack into the snow. Sentry reeled in the cable: the far end had been severed cleanly, as if cut by hydraulic shears.
incidents.tactical_action: Tether replaced with high-tensile chain; fuel vault access restricted.

incidents.title: Stationary Red Light on Lake Tessarat
incidents.log_entry: 23:10 — Sentry observed a single bright ruby-red pinpoint of light hovering approximately one meter above the frozen surface of Lake Tessarat, four kilometers out. Light was steady, unblinking, and cast a long, narrow red reflection across the black ice. Through the optical telescope, the light appeared to be a glowing spherical bead approximately the size of a walnut, suspended in mid-air with no pole, wire, or balloon visible. At 00:45, the light slowly drifted three hundred meters to the east at walking speed, paused above the sunken church spire for ten minutes, and then vanished. Temperature on the ice at that hour was minus forty-four degrees. Sentry recorded azimuth 034 degrees.
incidents.tactical_action: Azimuth logged; lake patrols warned to avoid Spire sector.

incidents.title: Vibrating Soil at Post 9
incidents.log_entry: 05:50 — While clearing ice from the gate hinges, sentry felt the frozen ground under his boots vibrating at a high, smooth frequency resembling an electric gyrocompass or heavy flywheel. Sentry pressed a wooden spade handle against his ear and placed the blade on the snow: the sound of complex, precision brass clockwork ticking and gear trains meshing could be heard clearly from approximately two meters beneath the dirt. There are no municipal pipes, tunnels, or bunkers recorded at this sector on any pre-war civil defense map. Sentry marked the spot with a red flag. When we returned with excavation picks at noon, the vibration had ceased and the soil was silent.
incidents.tactical_action: Sector flagged on engineering map as Anomaly 9.

incidents.title: Sudden Warm Air Inflow at 02:00
incidents.log_entry: 02:14 — While standing watch in the unheated cupola with frost thick on the periscope glass, the temperature inside the chamber suddenly rose from minus thirty-five degrees to plus twenty-two degrees Celsius within the span of thirty seconds. The frost on the glass melted into running water; the sentry's breath stopped frosting; and the air in the cupola smelled strongly of damp summer loam, freshly cut grass, and ozone. Sentry checked the external thermocouple: outside the hatch, the blizzard was raging at minus thirty-four degrees. The warm condition persisted for four minutes and eighteen seconds, then collapsed back to sub-zero freeze in less than ten seconds, instantly refreezing the water droplets on the periscope into clear ice beads. Sentry sat in silence until relieved.
incidents.tactical_action: Thermal sensor calibrated; sealed chamber inspected for vents.

incidents.weather_conditions: Clear dawn, +4°C, gentle spring wind, morning birdsong
incidents.title: The First Morning Without a Mask
incidents.log_entry: 05:30 — I stood the morning watch on the new wooden tower above the meadow. For the first time in ten years, I did not wear the rubber respirator or carry the dosimeter on my belt. The air smelled of wet earth and melting pine needles. Looking north across the valley, the mist was rising off the canal. No figures standing in the whiteout; no ghost convoys on the highway; no phantom knocks on the iron doors. Just forty chimneys sending clean grey smoke into a blue sky. I closed the Night Watch Logbook, tied the oilcloth ribbon around the cover, and placed it on the library shelf beside Dr. Vel's triage records. The watch is relieved. The morning has come.
incidents.tactical_action: Surface sentry roster permanently decommissioned; log archived.
